Summary: Fix Kafka topic-per-room and shared-consumer-group scaling gap (CHAT-24)
Description: Current Kafka implementation publishes per-room-per-event-type topics and uses a shared consumer group for all ws-gateway pods. This does not scale to CHAT-24's ~7,000 concurrent rooms (impractical topic/partition count) and breaks multi-pod ws-gateway delivery (consumer groups split partitions, not broadcast). Runtime bug (dispatch errors from unhandled payload types) has been fixed as a stopgap: no-op @KafkaHandler(isDefault=true) methods added to ReceiptEventListener (chat-service) and RoomEventBroadcastListener (ws-gateway) to suppress consumer-side errors on unknown event types. This stopgap stops errors but does not fix the underlying issue: listeners still wildcard-subscribe to all events and silently no-op on unhandled types. Actual scope: implement bounded per-event-type topic set with roomId/userId partition key, per-pod consumer identity, and narrower per-service topic patterns (no more shared wildcard subscriptions) as documented in docs/solution-architecture.md § 'Messaging backbone scaling'. Reference: CHAT-113.

Summary: solution-architecture.md's Kafka event catalog section doesn't match real event/topic contracts
Description: The 'Kafka event catalog and examples' subsection under 'Chat Rooms & Messaging (CHAT-104 / FR-02)' documents an event envelope (eventId, eventType, aggregateType, aggregateId, version, payload wrapper) and example events (chattera.events.room-message-created without roomId suffix, room-message-delivered, room-message-read, room-member-joined, presence-updated, file-uploaded) that do not match implementation. Actual DomainEvent records are flat with only occurredAt() method, no envelope; actual topic names include roomId suffix (chattera.events.room-message-created.<roomId>) and receipts use chattera.events.receipt.delivered/read; events like room-member-joined, presence-updated, file-uploaded don't exist in codebase (file-service is scaffold only, presence is Redis key write not Kafka event). Section reads as current reality but is aspirational/incorrect throughout. Correct the section to match actual event/topic contracts and current implementation.
